claims.text: Local compositional heterogeneity governs the premelting behavior of HEA nanoparticles.
Local compositional heterogeneity governs the melting behavior of HEA nanoparticles.
Local compositional heterogeneity influences atomic bonding strength.
Local compositional heterogeneity influences the distribution of surface energy.
Uniform and segregated elemental distributions can serve as controlled low- and high-heterogeneity states.
Heterogeneous regions produce spatial variations in atomic bonding strength.
Heterogeneous regions produce spatial variations in surface energy.
Variations in bonding strength and surface energy lower the energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
Lower diffusion barriers destabilize the nanoparticle lattice and initiate premelting.
Nanoparticles with greater compositional heterogeneity will have an earlier premelting onset than uniformly distributed nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with greater compositional heterogeneity will have lower melting temperatures than uniformly distributed nanoparticles.
Uniformly distributed HEA nanoparticles are expected to exhibit delayed premelting and higher melting temperatures.
The proposed relationship holds for HEA nanoparticles with diameters from 1 to 100 nm.
The proposed relationship holds when entropy dominates enthalpic contributions to phase stability.
The magnitude of the heterogeneity effect may depend on the elemental combination and atomic-size mismatch.
DSC and in situ TEM heating can be used to compare premelting onset and melting temperatures between uniform and heterogeneous nanoparticles.
Failure of the heterogeneous particles to show both earlier premelting and lower melting temperatures would falsify the hypothesis.
